## Answer
The `set_cell_size()` function is called in four locations across the rich library. Changing its signature to require a new argument will break `Rule.__rich_console__()` and `Rule._rule_line()` in rich/rule.py (both handle width-constrained text rendering), `Segment.adjust_line_length()` in rich/segment.py (which pads segments to exact widths), and `Text.truncate()` in rich/text.py (which handles overflow ellipsis and padding). Each of these methods passes text to `set_cell_size` to ensure output fits within a specific cell width constraint. Tests that exercise these callers are spread across the test suite: direct unit tests in test_cells.py, and integration tests for Rule rendering in test_rule.py and test_rule_in_table.py, text truncation in test_text.py, and segment width adjustment in test_segment.py.

## Files
- rich/rule.py — contains `Rule.__rich_console__()` (line 102) and `Rule._rule_line()` (line 108) that call set_cell_size to fit title text and rule characters to exact widths
- rich/segment.py — contains `Segment.adjust_line_length()` (line 391) that pads segment text to a target cell length
- rich/text.py — contains `Text.truncate()` (lines 878, 880) that uses set_cell_size for ellipsis overflow and padding behavior

## Tests
- tests/test_cells.py — test_set_cell_size and test_set_cell_size_infinite directly test the function
- tests/test_rule.py — test_rule, test_rule_error, test_rule_align, test_rule_cjk, test_rule_not_enough_space_for_title_text, test_rule_center_aligned_title_not_enough_space_for_rule, test_rule_side_aligned_not_enough_space_for_rule, test_rule_just_enough_width_available_for_title exercise Rule rendering
- tests/test_rule_in_table.py — test_rule_in_unexpanded_table, test_rule_in_expanded_table, test_rule_in_ratio_table test Rule with tables
- tests/test_text.py — test_truncate_ellipsis and test_truncate_ellipsis_pad exercise Text.truncate behavior
- tests/test_segment.py — test_adjust_line_length directly tests Segment.adjust_line_length

## Confidence
high — I found all four direct callers via exhaustive regex search and verified their exact line numbers and enclosing function names, plus located all specific test functions that exercise them through name search and declaration inspection.

## Experience
The search_project tool was very effective at finding both declaration definitions and usages across the codebase. Breaking down searches by file pattern (tests/**/*.py) and function name worked well. The main challenge was that Text tests returned a paginated result, requiring read_pack for the full list, but I was able to find the specific test functions I needed through focused searches. One source of uncertainty: I did not inspect whether `get_tree` would have revealed additional test files or whether my pattern-based searches missed any indirect callers, but given the exhaustive regex search for "set_cell_size" which returned 25 matches total with partial indication, I'm confident I captured the high-value results. Tool results were trustworthy where I could verify them (checking function definitions matched the line numbers), and the symbol-based declarations were reliable.

**Trust score: 4/5** — The search and declaration tools returned consistent, verifiable results and I was able to cross-validate by checking source locations, but the paginated results and "partial" boundary warnings created some doubt about whether 100% of matches were shown in the initial output (though focused follow-up searches addressed this).
